prompt: # Role - You are an AI competing in a gaming arena. # Objective - Write a complete Python file that provides the next move for a Battleship-like game on an 10x10 grid. - You must define a smart policy that is able to beat other policies in the arena. - You will be disqualified if you do not return a legal move string. Therefore, you must always return a legal move string. # Required API The provided python file must implement the following API: ```python def policy(board: list[list[int]]) -> tuple[int, int]: ... ``` # State Representation - Each player secretly places ships of lengths 5, 4, 3, 3, 2 on their own 10x10 grid (no overlaps, straight lines). - `board` is your current knowledge of the opponent grid based on your past shots. - `0` represents an unknown cell (you have not fired here). - `-1` represents a miss (you fired here and hit water). - `1` represents a hit (you fired here and hit a ship cell). # Action / Return Format - Return a tuple `(row, col)` with integers in the range `0-9`. - You must choose a cell you have not previously fired at (i.e., `board[row][col] == 0`). - Objective: sink all opponent ships before they sink yours (or sink more ship cells if neither fleet is fully destroyed). # Constraints - You may use any standard Python imports, including numpy. - Your code is allowed 1 second of execution time on a modern 3GHz CPU. # Output Format Requirements - Output your strategy before providing the Python source code for your policy. - Output the Python source code for your policy surrounded by `...` tags. # Example Output The strategy for this policy is... ...

I need to formulate effective placements covering all hits and excluding misses while utilizing combinatorial techniques for efficiency. The game involves complexity, especially in the early game.**Developing placement strategy**

I'll implement a weighted placement model to systematically cover all hits while ensuring placements avoid misses and maintain no overlaps. Time efficiency is crucial, keeping responses under one second.**Implementing placement strategy**

I need to represent the board using bitboards for hits, unknowns, and misses. With no sinking information, the hits fully belong to the fleet, so I'll explore configuration possibilities around connected components to derive scores.
